title: Config schema + validation for Dedicated pool configs (lint + policy gates + break-glass)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Implement a versioned JSON schema + validation pipeline for Dedicated pool configs used by fleet provisioning (and later drift detection). This is a hard gate before provisioning begins, with an audited break-glass mechanism for edge cases.

Context
We repeatedly lose time during pool bring-up due to small config errors (bad CIDR, mismatched region, missing pinned chart versions, unsafe runtime flags, etc.). This ticket defines:
1) the schema (fields, defaults, versioning)
2) lint + policy checks (human-friendly errors)
3) a break-glass override that is explicit, admin-only, and logged

Primary consumers
- Fleet Provisioner service (orchestration)
- Operator CLI (dry-run/validate)
- Control plane API (create/update pool config)

References
- ADR-0143: Config validation + policy gates
- Confluence: provision-to-ready pipeline overview (validation stage)

Proposed approach
- JSON Schema for structural validation (draft 2020-12)
- Separate policy layer for cross-field and environment-specific constraints
- Output: a deterministic list of validation findings with stable codes (for dashboards + alerting)

Out of scope
- Building a full UI config editor
- Removing ability to do manual override entirely (we need an escape hatch during pilot, but it must be auditable)

Owners
- Eng: Benji Okafor (schema + rules), Jordan Lee (policy engine), Rafael Mendes (SRE signoff for gating behavior)
- Security consult: Kevin Osei (audit requirements)
acceptance_criteria:
Schema + validation
- Pool configs have an explicit schemaVersion field and validate against the published JSON Schema.
- Validation can run in: (a) CLI dry-run, (b) provisioning service pre-flight, and (c) control plane API on write.
- Validation failures return actionable, operator-readable errors with: finding code, summary, field path, and remediation hint.

Policy gates
- Implement initial rule set covering known footguns:
  - Region/zone constraints: declared region must match pool placement / networking region.
  - CIDR validation: disallow overlaps with Redwood-reserved ranges; enforce / size bounds.
  - GPU SKU guardrails: SKU must be in allowed list per region; block unsupported combinations.
  - Runtime / chart pinning: require explicit runtimeChartVersion + runtimeImageVersion (no floating tags).
  - Helm values safety: block known-dangerous knobs (e.g., disabling TLS, disabling node taints, turning off readiness gates).
  - Autoscaling bounds: minReplicas <= maxReplicas; enforce sane caps and step sizes.
  - Observability required fields: ensure stage events/metrics aren’t disabled.

Break-glass
- Admin-only override to bypass policy gates (NOT schema structural validation).
- Override requires: reason string + ticket/link (Linear/Jira) + actor identity.
- Override is logged to audit log with correlation_id and surfaced as a structured provisioning event.
- Override triggers an alert/hook (non-paging) to #eng-sre and creates a breadcrumb in the provisioning run details.

Testing + rollout
- Unit tests for schema + policy rules with representative configs (good/bad).
- Integration test: provisioning run fails fast on invalid config before any Terraform apply.
- Docs: add examples of common failures and how to remediate; include break-glass procedure.
- Rollout behind feature flag in staging first; production enablement only after SRE signoff.
implementation_notes:
Schema design (v1)
- Top-level fields (initial):
  - schemaVersion (string, required, e.g., "1.0")
  - poolId (string, required)
  - customerId (string, required)
  - environment (enum: staging|prod)
  - region (string, required)
  - gpuSku (string, required)
  - nodeCount / capacity (object-like semantics but represented in schema as explicit fields where possible to keep diffs readable)
  - networking: vpcId/subnetIds OR networkProfileRef (depending on deployment mode)
  - runtime:
    - runtimeChartVersion (string)
    - runtimeImageVersion (string)
    - configFlags (map of string->string; policy-enforced allowlist)
  - autoscaling:
    - enabled (bool)
    - minReplicas/maxReplicas
  - observability:
    - metricsEnabled (bool)
    - logsEnabled (bool)
    - tracingEnabled (bool)
  - readiness:
    - gatesEnabled (bool)
    - perfCanaryEnabled (bool)
    - perfThresholdProfile (string)

Validator architecture
- Library/package: control-plane repo shared module "poolconfig" (Go)
  - ValidateSchema(configBytes) -> findings
  - ValidatePolicy(config, ctx) -> findings
  - Findings include: code (stable), severity (error|warning), path, message, hint
- Context (ctx) includes environment/region catalogs (allowed SKUs, reserved CIDRs, etc.) loaded from a versioned data file to avoid hardcoding.

Break-glass behavior
- Break-glass only bypasses policy errors (severity=error) when override is present and actor is authorized.
- Structural/schema errors always block.
- Override object contains:
  - overrideId (generated)
  - actor (from auth context)
  - reason (required)
  - reference (required: Linear/Jira URL)
  - expiresAt (required; default max 24h)
- Every override emits:
  - Audit log entry (who/what/when/why + config hash)
  - Provisioning event: config_validation_overridden

Error messaging
- Prefer actionable hints (“Set runtimeChartVersion explicitly; floating tags are blocked. Example: runtimeChartVersion: 1.18.3”).
- Ensure error codes are stable for dashboards/alerting:
  - CFG001 schema_invalid_json
  - CFG010 missing_required_field
  - POL100 cidr_overlap_reserved
  - POL120 region_mismatch
  - POL130 sku_not_allowed
  - POL200 unpinned_version
  - POL240 unsafe_helm_value
  - OVR900 override_required_fields_missing

Docs + examples
- Provide:
  - Minimal valid config example for staging and prod
  - Common failure examples
  - Break-glass playbook snippet (who can approve, how to request, how it’s logged)

Security considerations
- Ensure override is admin-only and requires least-privilege role.
- Audit log is immutable and queryable; include correlation_id from provisioning run.
- Do not log full secrets in config; schema should reject fields commonly used to inline secrets (policy: block keys matching /secret|token|password/i unless explicitly allowlisted for non-sensitive).

comments: 2025-02-20 (Vanessa Ortiz): Marking as P0 for sprint. We’ve had 3+ incidents where a small config typo turns into hours of debug post-provisioning. We need a hard pre-flight gate with an escape hatch that doesn’t become the default path.

2025-02-21 (Benji Okafor): Drafted schema outline and initial rule list from operator pain points + config-schema brainstorm doc. Next step is deciding what’s “schema” vs “policy”. Proposal: JSON Schema for structure/types + policy layer for region/SKU/cross-field constraints.

2025-02-22 (Jordan Lee): +1 on splitting policy from schema. For policy engine, recommend stable finding codes and a strict no-network-call rule (load catalogs locally). Also: schema should reject unknown top-level keys to prevent silently ignored settings.

2025-02-25 (Rafael Mendes): From SRE side: schema validation should run before Terraform. Fail fast, no resources created. Break-glass must page nobody by default but must be visible (Slack + dashboard) so we can track how often we’re bypassing gates.

2025-02-27 (Kevin Osei): Break-glass requirements: (1) actor identity, (2) reason, (3) linked ticket, (4) expiration, (5) config hash. Also ensure we don’t allow bypass of schema validation; only policy. Please include an explicit audit log record type so we can filter/report.

2025-03-03 (Benji Okafor): Implemented schema v1 + validator interface in control plane module. Added initial rules: pinned versions, CIDR sanity, region/SKU allowlist, and a basic blocklist for unsafe runtime flags. Pushed PR-48235 for review.

2025-03-06 (Jordan Lee): Review feedback on PR-48235: (a) add field-paths in findings using JSONPointer-style (e.g., /runtime/runtimeChartVersion), (b) ensure stable ordering of findings for deterministic CLI output, (c) add unit test coverage for unknown-key rejection. Benji addressing.
2025-03-09 (Benji Okafor): Added break-glass support behind admin-only endpoint. Override bypasses only policy errors and emits audit logs + provisioning event. PR-48236 up.

2025-03-11 (Rafael Mendes): Tested staging provisioning with invalid config: correctly blocks before Terraform. Tested override path: works, but please ensure Slack message includes the Linear link and the expiresAt timestamp so oncall can follow up. Also recommend a warning banner in run status payload (“validation overridden”).

2025-03-14 (Benji Okafor): Added “validation_overridden=true” flag to run status output + included expiresAt + reference URL in the event payload. Updated docs/examples in repo. Marking ready for merge once Kevin approves audit format.
2025-03-18 (Vanessa Ortiz): Merged PRs; feature flag enabled in staging. Tracking override usage separately; any override during pilot needs to be raised in the daily standup. Marking ticket Done.
